name: IL-13
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by 5 points on the partisan baseline
Incumbent Nikki Budzinski has a massive financial edge ($2.6M cash vs. $12K)
Prediction markets price Democratic win at 96%
No public polling or expert ratings to refine the estimate
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Budzinski: a D+5 district, incumbency, and a lopsided fundraising advantage over Jeff Wilson, who has raised little and has almost no cash on hand. Markets agree, pricing her at 96%, so the forecast stays near the fundamentals-based margin with only a slight trim for the absence of polling.
model.watch: Any late surge of outside Republican spending or a polling surprise showing Wilson within single digits would warrant a downgrade.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
First-term incumbent Nikki Budzinski seeks reelection in an Illinois district that leans Democratic by about five points. She has raised nearly $2.9 million and holds $2.6 million on hand, while Republican Jeff Wilson has raised about $348,000 with only $12,000 remaining, leaving him little capacity to compete on the airwaves.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the incumbent's financial dominance, and prediction markets, which price a Democratic win at 96 percent. The race is rated Safe Democratic, with the main uncertainty coming from the lack of direct polling rather than any specific evidence of a competitive contest.
